components.gap: ED26-P15-CH-martingales-and-convergence-C002: the source's interpretive and terminological claims in Example 4.2.1 (PTE5 pp. 217-218) are not supplied: for mu <= 0 the supermartingale S_n corresponds to betting on an unfavorable game, so there is nothing super about a supermartingale; the name comes from superharmonic functions f (continuous derivatives of order <= 2 and sum of the second partial derivatives <= 0), which satisfy the mean-value inequality f(x) >= |B(x,r)|^{-1} times the integral of f over the ball B(x,r) = {y : |x - y| <= r} (source display (4.2.1)). The linear, quadratic, product and exponential constructions themselves are complete (body 35-63, annex 3-63). def:p15-martingale-next (body 359-360) only records that this explanation is not a premise of the results, which excludes it rather than treating it.

ED26-P15-CH-martingales-and-convergence-C005: the source's interpretation and justification of predictable sequences and of the transform (PTE5 p. 219) are not supplied: H_n is the amount a gambler bets at time n, which may depend on the outcomes at times 1, ..., n-1 but not on the outcome at time n; X_n is the net amount won by betting one dollar each time, and (H.X)_n is the winnings of the system H because a wager of 3 dollars changes the fortune three times as much as a wager of 1 dollar; alternatively X_m is the value of a stock and H_m the number of shares held from time m-1 to time m. def:p15-predictable-transform (body 93-104) gives the measurability condition, the formula and a title only.

duties.duty: ED26-P15-CH-martingales-and-convergence-C001 (partial): Hypotheses and source variant are not supplied (failure condition: unstated assumption). def:p15-filtration-martingale (body 18-26) defines adaptedness but never requires it. A martingale is therefore any real process with integrable terms and E(X_{n+1}|F_n)=X_n, and sub/supermartingales swap the identity for an inequality. The held source's definition (Durrett PTE5 p. 217) has three conditions, and condition (ii), 'X_n adapted to F_n', is dropped. For sub- and supermartingales the inequality does not imply adaptedness. The handbook's own proofs still rely on it: annex 77 says 'The case n=m follows from adaptedness', annex 91 says 'adaptedness was explicitly assumed', and annex 35/104/124/150/412/559/586/734 check adaptedness. The optional-stopping chapter on the same route states the convention outright (optional-stopping-and-random-walks.tex 12-13). Concrete case: take F_n trivial, X_0=-2-U and X_n=-1 for n>=1. This meets the definition as written, but the n=m case of thm:p15-martingale-conditioning fails.
duties.gap: Not resolved at the cited location: def:p15-filtration-martingale (body 18-26) still never requires adaptedness; the owned convention and the owned counterexample theorem are a separate later chapter that contradicts the entry; amend the read-only definition (lead).
